# Citations

Sources for [`analysis.md`](analysis.md) and the per-dimension reference files
under [`references/`](references/). Tiers:

- **Tier 1:** Peer-reviewed papers, government/institutional reports
- **Tier 2:** Manufacturer specs, established reference sites, university publications
- **Tier 3:** Industry blogs, conference talks, well-known practitioners
- **Tier 4:** Forums, personal blogs, GitHub discussions, social media

---

**[1]** "StatefulSets." *Kubernetes Documentation*, 2026.
<https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/statefulset/>
**Tier:** 2
Canonical reference for StatefulSet behavior. Quoted: "Deleting and/or
scaling a StatefulSet down will _not_ delete the volumes associated with
the StatefulSet. This is done to ensure data safety, which is generally
more valuable than an automatic purge of all related StatefulSet
resources." PVC naming convention `{volumeClaimTemplate.metadata.name}-{pod-ordinal}`.
StatefulSets selected when workloads require "stable, unique network
identifiers" or "stable, persistent storage."

**[2]** "Kubernetes 1.27: StatefulSet PVC Auto-Deletion (beta)."
*Kubernetes Blog*, 2023-05-04.
<https://kubernetes.io/blog/2023/05/04/kubernetes-1-27-statefulset-pvc-auto-deletion-beta/>
**Tier:** 2
`persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy` graduated alpha in 1.23, beta in
1.27. Default is `whenDeleted: Retain, whenScaled: Retain` matching
legacy behavior. With both set to `Delete`, "PVCs are deleted immediately
when their replica is no longer needed. Note this does not include when
a Pod is deleted and a new version rescheduled... The PVC is deleted
only when the replica is no longer needed as signified by a scale-down
or StatefulSet deletion."

**[3]** "Persistent Volumes." *Kubernetes Documentation*, 2026.
<https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes/>
**Tier:** 2
PV/PVC lifecycle. "If a user deletes a PVC in active use by a Pod, the
PVC is not removed immediately. PVC removal is postponed until the PVC
is no longer actively used by any Pods" (Storage Object in Use
Protection). Under `Retain`, "the volume is not available for another
claim because the previous claimant's data remains on the volume." Under
`Delete`, "deletion removes both the PersistentVolume object from
Kubernetes, as well as the associated storage asset."

**[4]** "Delete a StatefulSet." *Kubernetes Documentation*, 2026.
<https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/delete-stateful-set/>
**Tier:** 2
Quoted: "Deleting the Pods in a StatefulSet will not delete the
associated volumes. This is to ensure that you have the chance to copy
data off the volume before deleting it." "Use caution when deleting a
PVC, as it may lead to data loss." Notes that deleting the PVC
afterward "might trigger deletion of the backing Persistent Volumes
depending on the storage class and reclaim policy."

**[5]** "Pod Security Standards." *Kubernetes Documentation*, 2026.
<https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/>
**Tier:** 2
Authoritative profile definitions. Restricted requires:
`allowPrivilegeEscalation=false`, `runAsNonRoot=true`,
`capabilities.drop=ALL`, `seccompProfile.type=RuntimeDefault` or
`Localhost`. Volume types restricted to: `configMap`, `csi`, `downwardAPI`,
`emptyDir`, `ephemeral`, `persistentVolumeClaim`, `projected`, `secret`.
Baseline has no such requirements.

**[6]** "Configure a Security Context for a Pod or Container."
*Kubernetes Documentation*, 2026.
<https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/>
**Tier:** 2
`fsGroup` and `fsGroupChangePolicy` semantics. fsGroup affects volume
ownership and "all processes of the container are also part of the
supplementary group ID." `fsGroupChangePolicy` values: `Always` and
`OnRootMismatch`.

**[7]** "Kubernetes 1.20: Granular Control of Volume Permission and
Ownership Changes." *Kubernetes Blog*, 2020-12-14.
<https://kubernetes.io/blog/2020/12/14/kubernetes-release-1.20-fsgroupchangepolicy-fsgrouppolicy/>
**Tier:** 2
Original `fsGroupChangePolicy` announcement. Quoted: the recursive chown
"can be pretty expensive for larger volumes with lots of small files,
which causes pod startup to take a long time." `OnRootMismatch`:
"if the root of the volume already has the correct permissions, the
recursive permission change can be skipped." Notes that multi-writer
volumes (NFS, Gluster) may not support `chown()`/`chmod()`.

**[8]** "Kubernetes 1.26: Passing Pod fsGroup to CSI Drivers At Mount Time."
*Kubernetes Blog*, 2022-12-23.
<https://kubernetes.io/blog/2022/12/23/kubernetes-12-06-fsgroup-on-mount/>
**Tier:** 2
`DelegateFSGroupToCSIDriver`: alpha 1.22, beta 1.25, GA 1.26. When the
CSI driver applies fsGroup at mount, "neither `.spec.fsGroupPolicy` for
the CSIDriver object, nor `.spec.securityContext.fsGroupChangePolicy`
for the Pod" has effect.

**[9]** "Support for fsGroup-based ownership and permission management."
*Kubernetes CSI Developer Documentation*, n.d.
<https://kubernetes-csi.github.io/docs/support-fsgroup.html>
**Tier:** 2
CSIDriver `fsGroupPolicy` values:
- `None`: "volumes will be mounted with no modifications, as the CSI
  volume driver does not support these operations."
- `File`: kubelet may apply fsGroup "regardless of fstype or access mode."
- `ReadWriteOnceWithFSType`: "Changes will only occur if the `fsType`
  is defined and the persistent volume's `accessModes` contains
  `ReadWriteOnce`."

**[10]** "PVC Ownership and Permission." *Longhorn Documentation*, 1.11.0.
<https://longhorn.io/docs/1.11.0/nodes-and-volumes/volumes/pvc-ownership-and-permission/>
**Tier:** 2
Longhorn CSI sets `fsGroupPolicy: ReadWriteOnceWithFSType`. Filesystem
mode: "the Kubelet attempts to change the ownership and permission of a
Longhorn PVC." Block mode: "Kubelet never attempts to change the
permission and ownership of the block device... Longhorn puts the block
device into group id 6, which is typically associated with the 'disk'
group." Pods using block-mode PVCs "must either set the group id 6 in
the `pod.spec.securityContext`, or run as root."

**[11]** "Troubleshooting: Volumes take a long time to finish mounting."
*Longhorn Documentation*, n.d.
<https://longhorn.io/kb/troubleshooting-volume-take-long-time-to-mount/>
**Tier:** 2
Documents recursive chown delay on large Longhorn volumes. Mitigation
guidance: pair `fsGroup` with `fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch`.

**[12]** "StatefulSet PersistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy not deleting
PVCs when WhenScaled: Delete is used." *GitHub kubernetes/kubernetes*,
issue #126919, 2024-08-26.
<https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126919>
**Tier:** 4
Bug: `WhenScaled: Delete` fails to delete PVCs on scale-down when the
`OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement` admission plugin is enabled.
Error: "could not update claim ... for delete policy ownerRefs:
persistentvolumeclaims ... is forbidden: cannot set blockOwnerDeletion
if an ownerReference refers to a resource you can't set finalizers on."
Closed via PR #126920.

**[13]** "Pod with very large CSI volume took 40 hours to finish applying
fsgroup." *GitHub kubernetes/kubernetes*, issue #118058.
<https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/118058>
**Tier:** 4
"A pod was created with fsgroup and a very large CSI volume that ended
up taking 40 hours to finish applying fsgroup." Subsequent pod
redeploy with `fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch` "remained blocked
waiting for the first pod's mount to complete, as volume operations are
serialized per volume." Only documented workaround: "restart kubelet so
that the go routines would be cleared."

**[14]** "Cannot read/write to block volume as non-root."
*GitHub longhorn/longhorn*, issue #8088.
<https://github.com/longhorn/longhorn/issues/8088>
**Tier:** 4
Non-root pods cannot access Longhorn block volumes: `dd: failed to open
'/dev/longhorn/testblk': Permission denied`. Device shows as
`brw-rw---- 1 root root`. Solutions discussed but not definitively
recommended: CSI-level chown, init container, or supplementalGroups
escalation.

**[15]** "Init containers in restricted namespace." *Discuss Kubernetes
forum*, thread #30797.
<https://discuss.kubernetes.io/t/init-containers-in-restricted-namespace/30797>
**Tier:** 4
Confirmation that init containers under PodSecurity `restricted` cannot
run as root because every container (including init) must satisfy
`runAsNonRoot=true`. The `chown -R` init pattern is incompatible with
restricted without relaxing to `baseline` or carving a PSA exemption.

**[16]** "Expose a tailnet service to your Kubernetes cluster (cluster
egress)." *Tailscale Docs*, 2026-01-05.
<https://tailscale.com/docs/features/kubernetes-operator/how-to/cluster-egress>
**Tier:** 2
Egress pattern: `ExternalName` Service annotated with
`tailscale.com/tailnet-fqdn` (or `tailscale.com/tailnet-ip`). The
operator creates a proxy Pod (StatefulSet) plus a headless Service,
then mutates `spec.externalName` to "the Kubernetes DNS name of another
Kubernetes Service that is fronting the egress proxy in `tailscale`
namespace." Quoted: "Exposing tailnet services to your Kubernetes
cluster is currently in beta."

**[17]** "Kubernetes operator." *Tailscale Docs*, 2026-01-05.
<https://tailscale.com/docs/features/kubernetes-operator>
**Tier:** 2
Operator architecture. Proxies deploy as "a StatefulSet in the
operator's namespace (defaults to `tailscale`)." "Custom routing and
forwarding rules in each proxy Pod's network namespace only" — no host
iptables changes.

**[18]** "Tailscale Kubernetes Operator Architecture." *GitHub
tailscale/tailscale*, main branch.
<https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/blob/main/docs/k8s/operator-architecture.md>
**Tier:** 2
Upstream architecture doc. Egress pattern: "The user deploys a Service
with type: ExternalName and an annotation
tailscale.com/tailnet-fqdn: db.tails-scales.ts.net. The operator creates
a proxy Pod managed by a single replica StatefulSet, and a headless
Service pointing at the proxy Pod." The operator then "updates the
ExternalName Service's spec.externalName field to point at the headless
Service it created in the previous step." Proxy Pod uses "iptables or
nftables rules to DNAT traffic bound for the proxy's tailnet IP."

**[19]** "Catastrophic perf collapse with k3s + Flannel over Tailscale +
Tailscale operator." *GitHub tailscale/tailscale*, issue #16820.
<https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/16820>
**Tier:** 4
"2-3 Mbit/s for iperf3 TCP, versus 700-800 Mbit/s directly to the k8s
node's Tailscale address." Root cause: MTU mismatch — Tailscale
interface MTU is 1280, container interfaces inside the cluster default
to 1500, and WireGuard encapsulation requires >1280 MTU to carry 1280
MTU payloads. Documented workaround: "lower MTU to 1200 on at least one
end of the connection."

**[20]** "Established TCP connections do not gracefully fail over when
ProxyGroup replica restarts." *GitHub tailscale/tailscale*, issue #16162.
<https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/16162>
**Tier:** 4
Quoted: "if an established database connection (let's say it's routed
through proxy-ha-0) is interrupted because proxy-ha-0 restarts for any
reason (like an upgrade or configuration change), the database
connection will continuously resend data until it times out." **Status:
Closed as not planned** — Tailscale has elected not to fix this failure
mode.

**[21]** Selent, Stefan. "gRPC and Tailscale: A 30-second mystery."
*stefan-selent.dev*, 2025-12-18.
<https://stefan-selent.dev/2025/12/18/grpc-and-tailscale.html>
**Tier:** 3
gRPC's default `dns:///` URI scheme triggers client-side load-balancing
DNS lookup that "times out" through Tailscale's resolver, adding ~30s on
first connect. Fix: `passthrough:///` URI scheme that "skips this
lookup and directly feeds the hostname into the OS." The post is
specific to Temporal CLI; the underlying resolver mechanism is the same
mechanism OTLP gRPC clients use.

**[22]** "Network Policies." *Kubernetes Documentation*, 2026.
<https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/>
**Tier:** 2
NetworkPolicy spec. "IP blocks (exception: traffic to and from the node
where a Pod is running is always allowed, regardless of the IP address
of the Pod or the node)." AND vs OR semantics: "A single `to`/`from`
entry that specifies both `namespaceSelector` and `podSelector` selects
particular Pods within particular namespaces" (AND). Two separate
entries in the array are OR'd. "Network policies do not conflict; they
are additive."

**[23]** "Namespaces." *Kubernetes Documentation*, 2026.
<https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/namespaces/>
**Tier:** 2
Auto-injected label. Quoted: "The Kubernetes control plane sets an
immutable label `kubernetes.io/metadata.name` on all namespaces. The
value of the label is the namespace name."

**[24]** "Networking Services." *K3s Documentation*, 2026.
<https://docs.k3s.io/networking/networking-services>
**Tier:** 2
"K3s includes an embedded network policy controller. The underlying
implementation is kube-router's netpol controller library (no other
kube-router functionality is present)." The `--disable-network-policy`
flag disables the controller. Disabling does not remove the existing
iptables rules.

**[25]** "Basic Network Options." *K3s Documentation*, 2026.
<https://docs.k3s.io/networking/basic-network-options>
**Tier:** 2
Default CNI is Flannel (vxlan backend). Example CIDR values:
`--cluster-cidr=10.42.0.0/16 --service-cidr=10.43.0.0/16`. To swap CNI:
`--flannel-backend=none --disable-network-policy`.

**[26]** "Network Policies in K3s." *SUSE Communities*, 2023-03-27.

**Tier:** 3
"The Flannel CNI doesn't support network polices." K3s uses

**[28]** "OpenTelemetry Collector Helm Chart Values."
*GitHub open-telemetry/opentelemetry-helm-charts*, main branch.
<https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-helm-charts/blob/main/charts/opentelemetry-collector/values.yaml>
**Tier:** 2
Default OTLP ports: 4317 (gRPC, `appProtocol: grpc`), 4318 (HTTP). Chart
ships `networkPolicy.enabled: false` by default; when enabled the chart
covers ingress with optional `egressRules`. Common label hooks
`additionalLabels: {}`, `podLabels: {}` available but no static labels
visible in the values file (templates apply them).

**Tier:** 2
Confirms kube-router enforces NetworkPolicy via iptables/ipsets in
